newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Oct 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Oct 8.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A total of 1,543 municipal mayors all over the country will meet starting today for a two-day national convention to press the national government for the immediate return of full supervision and control over the local police force. (MANILA BULLETIN)
- Members of the ruling party issued contradictory stands on the current campaign to amend the Constitution that will allow President Ramos to extend his six-year term.(PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)

- Governor Nur Misuari, newly-elected head of the Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao, said he will campaign for proportionate representation for Mindanao in Congress and the extension of the terms of elected government officials.(THE MANILA CHRONICLE)
- Anxiety over prospects for the local property sector and the general decline in most Asian markets gave portfolio investors enough reason to pull out of the local equities market. (BUSINESSWORLD)
- The Philippine peso will continue to be stable despite decline in interest rates, according to Central Bank Treasurer Sergio Edeza. (TODAY)

- Prospects of getting the retail trade liberalization bill passed this year turned bleak as opposition gained ground both in Congress and among various sectors of the economy. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
